category_total_desk_estimate_note: 42.9B + 35.3B + 4.6B at the CONSERVATIVE end of each byte anchor, and BEFORE any overlap deduction. Desk arithmetic over published aggregates, not measurement.
meets_3x_peak_demand_assessment: UNVERIFIED but very likely yes, with headroom. Requirement is 12B (3 x 4B peak). peS2o ALONE is 182.6 GB of UTF-8 text — to fall under 12B tokens it would have to tokenize at worse than 15.2 bytes/token, which is not physically plausible for English prose (real range 3.3-4.5). The same floor argument clears 12B on peS2o alone even at 0.07 tok/byte. So the pool is not at risk; what is unverified is the exact figure, and the direction of the error is toward MORE tokens than §3.2 claims, not fewer.
overlaps: peS2o and pubmed OVERLAP BY CONSTRUCTION and must not be naively summed. peS2o is derived from S2ORC, which ingests PubMed Central among its sources; and paper Table 4 shows peS2o's own field-of-study distribution is dominated by biomedicine — Medicine 2,435,244 docs (39.8% of the 6.1M train split) plus Biology 1,518,478 (24.8%). pubmed_filtered is 3,829,689 biomedical papers. The two corpora are drawing on a heavily shared population of open-access biomedical literature.

MITIGATING FACT, and it is a strong one: the Common Pile applied GLOBAL document-level fuzzy deduplication ACROSS ALL SOURCES (paper §4.1 — Dolma bloom filter, two docs are duplicates if they share >90% of their 20-grams). That is cross-source, not per-source, so exact and near-exact duplicate papers between peS2o and pubmed were already removed. UNRESOLVED: §4.1 describes the pipeline that produces the COMMA dataset, and Table 5/6 are captioned as the pipeline 'to construct the Comma dataset' — so it is not certain from the paper that the published _filtered repos are post-cross-source-dedup rather than post-per-source-filtering only. Verify before summing.

RESIDUAL HAZARD that dedup does NOT remove: the same paper reaching both corpora via different extraction pipelines. peS2o comes from Grobid over PDFs; pubmed comes from pandoc over nXML. Two renderings of one article can easily differ in more than 10% of their 20-grams (different boilerplate, table/figure handling, reference formatting) and would survive a 90%-of-20-grams filter as distinct documents. This is the same failure mode as the memory note on rephrased synthetic defeating n-gram dedup.

arxiv_papers_filtered is near-orthogonal to both — physics/math/CS LaTeX preprints, and Trafilatura-extracted rather than PDF- or XML-derived. peS2o Mathematics is only 135,676 docs and Physics 413,461, so the arXiv population is largely disjoint from peS2o's biomedical mass. Safe to add.
ArXiv Abstracts is a SEPARATE Common Pile source (2,504,679 docs / 2.4 GB) and is a strict subset-by-content of arxiv_papers for any paper in both — do not add it to this category as extra tokens.

Cross-category: none of these three overlaps the edu-web, code, math, or web categories' lineages. Common Pile is one of only three families the design doc §3.1 calls structurally near-orthogonal to CC-HTML.

partial_conversion_hazard.severity: HIGH — this is a bug in recount.py's estimator for this whole family, not a property of my category
partial_conversion_hazard.finding: All three academic corpora ship as .json.gz and datasets-server stopped its parquet conversion at the ~2.4 GB partial-conversion cap. /parquet returns partial=true with exactly 10 files against 48 / 17 / 8 real shards. Consequently /size num_rows counts ONLY THE CONVERTED HEAD: peS2o 165,031 rows vs 6,117,280 real docs (37.07x short), pubmed 163,259 vs 3,829,689 (23.46x), arxiv 78,823 vs 304,048 (3.86x).
partial_conversion_hazard.why_no_check_catches_it: recount.py multiplies by /size num_rows and treats it as exact ('^exact' in its own method string). Its stats_partial flag warns about a partial /statistics MEAN, not a partial ROW COUNT — nothing in the tool or the README distinguishes the two. So for any partially-converted corpus the tool silently reports the converted head's tokens as the corpus total, undercounting by the factors above. That is exactly the README's 'plausible number no check falsifies'.
partial_conversion_hazard.scope_beyond_this_category: Not limited to academic. common-pile/stackexchange_filtered and common-pile/github_archive_filtered (the QA and code categories) both show ~2.46 GB parquet_bytes in their result files — the same cap. Every common-pile source in §3.2 is likely affected, and so is any other .json.gz-hosted corpus.
partial_conversion_hazard.recommended_fix: Anchor on exact published whole-corpus UTF-8 bytes x measured tokens/byte, i.e. tokens = utf8_bytes x tokens_per_byte. Bytes need no mean-document-length term, are published exactly for all of Common Pile (paper Table 6, card-confirmed), and are immune to the converted head being length-biased. Keep the row-factor-rescaled figure as an independent cross-check: agreement means the head is representative, divergence means it is length-biased. Helper written to artifacts/recount/_academic_rescale.py — it needs only the per-source tokens_per_byte from a successful sample.

method_note: No dataset bytes were downloaded. All work here is datasets-server metadata calls (/size, /splits, /parquet, /statistics), the HF hub API (dataset_info, tree), the dataset cards, and the Common Pile paper PDF. No load_dataset, no hf_hub_download of a data file.
card_figure_provenance_finding: The single most reusable result from this category: §3.2's academic token figures are not tokenizer output of any kind. Paper Table 7's Tokens column equals Size(GB) x 0.25 for all 30 Common Pile sources (peS2o 182.6->45.65, PubMed 147.1->36.77, ArXiv Papers 19.5->4.88 — exact to two decimals). §3.2's 43.3B and 36.6B are those numbers. The design doc's warning that peS2o reports 'whitespace words' understates the problem: the figure in the table is a byte division, and it is not comparable to a dolma2 count for ANY Common Pile source. Every Common Pile row in §3.2 inherits this, so the correction is systematic rather than per-source.
